title: Wrap fetch network failures in a new `NetworkError` and stop retrying unknown errors
summary:
Ky now throws a new `NetworkError` (a `KyError` subclass) when `fetch` fails with a recognized network failure. Previously callers got the raw `TypeError`. The original error is on `error.cause`. The PR exports `NetworkError` and an `isNetworkError` type guard. It also changes the default retry logic: only `TimeoutError`, `HTTPError`, and `NetworkError` are retried. Any other error is thrown immediately unless `shouldRetry` returns `true`.

Detection uses `isRawNetworkError`, inlined from `is-network-error` v1.3.1. It matches a `TypeError` by runtime-specific message strings for Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Undici, Deno, Bun, and Cloudflare. A `try/catch` in the fetch path of `Ky.ts` performs the wrapping. Both the error type change and the narrowed retry policy break existing caller expectations. The PR also corrects stale JSDoc in `options.ts` and `retry.ts` about `maxRetryAfter` and timeout retries.

changes.what: The fetch call, with or without `timeout`, now sits in a `try/catch`. The catch rethrows `NetworkError(this.request, {cause})` when `isRawNetworkError` matches. The retry-delay logic now returns `#calculateDelay()` explicitly for timeouts and HTTP errors. It throws any error that is not `isNetworkError`.
changes.why: Callers and hooks now see `NetworkError` instead of `TypeError`. Errors that were retried before, such as arbitrary thrown errors from a custom `fetch`, are no longer retried by default.

changes.what: New `isRawNetworkError`. It checks for a `TypeError` whose message matches a known set of network-failure messages. It also handles special cases for Safari `Load failed`, Deno, and Chrome `Failed to fetch (host)`.
changes.why: This heuristic decides both wrapping and retry eligibility. An unmatched message means no wrapping and no retry.

changes.what: New `NetworkError extends KyError`. It has `name = 'NetworkError'`, a `request` property, and the message `Request failed due to a network error: METHOD URL`. It forwards `cause` to `super`.
changes.why: This is the new public error type for network failures.

changes.what: Adds `isNetworkError`, which checks `instanceof NetworkError` or `name === 'NetworkError'`. `isKyError` now also accepts `isNetworkError`.
changes.why: `Ky.ts` uses `isNetworkError` to decide retries. Users get a cross-realm guard.
This adds to the public API surface.

changes.what: Rewrites the `retry` JSDoc. It lists all retry fields and documents network-error retries. It also fixes the `maxRetryAfter` behavior description. It drops the delay formula and the outdated sentence 'Retries are not triggered following a timeout'.
JSDoc fixes for `maxRetryAfter`. The `shouldRetry` docs now state that unrecognized errors are not retried.
JSDoc for `beforeRetry` and `beforeError` now mentions `NetworkError` and `isNetworkError`.
Documents network-error retries and the `NetworkError` section with an example. It updates hook, `HTTPError`, and `KyError` text.
Adds tests for wrapping, default retry, POST non-retry, and non-network `TypeError` passthrough. It also covers `shouldRetry` forcing and fallthrough, `beforeError` cause chain, and `timeout: false`.
changes.why: These tests cover the new behavior.

changes.what: Simulated network failures now throw `TypeError('Failed to fetch')` instead of arbitrary messages. Assertions use `isNetworkError`.
changes.why: The old arbitrary messages are no longer recognized or retried. These test edits show the behavior change for custom `fetch` implementations.

changes.what: Reads the undici error code from `error.cause.cause` instead of `error.cause`.
changes.why: The extra `NetworkError` layer moves the cause one level deeper.
This reflects the new error type.

flow.caption: A fetch rejection passes through `isRawNetworkError`. Ky wraps recognized failures in `NetworkError`. The retry logic then retries only timeout, HTTP, or network errors.

risks.title: Network failures no longer surface as `TypeError`
risks.reason: Before this PR, a fetch network failure reached callers as the raw `TypeError`, for example with message `Failed to fetch`. Now callers receive a `NetworkError`, which is not a `TypeError`. Code that checks `error instanceof TypeError`, `error.message`, or `error.cause.code` breaks silently. The PR's own `test/headers.ts` edit shows this: the undici code moves from `error.cause` to `error.cause.cause`. This is a breaking change for callers.

risks.title: Unrecognized errors are no longer retried by default
risks.reason: The old code fell through to `#calculateDelay()` for any error. The new code throws anything that is not `isNetworkError`. Some failures never become a `NetworkError`. Examples are a network error from a runtime or fetch polyfill whose message is not in `isRawNetworkError`'s list, or a custom `fetch` that throws its own error type. Those failures now fail on the first attempt instead of retrying. The `test/hooks.ts` changes from `'network down'` to `'Failed to fetch'` show this regression.

risks.title: Name-based guard matches foreign `NetworkError` errors
risks.reason: `isNetworkError` returns true for any object with `name === 'NetworkError'`. Examples are a DOM `DOMException` named `NetworkError` or another library's error class. The retry logic would then retry such errors. `isKyError` would also misclassify them as Ky errors, even though they lack `request`.

tests.description: Use a custom `fetch` that throws `new Error('socket hang up')` with `retry: {limit: 2}`. Confirm it now runs once, where it ran three times before this PR. Decide whether that change is intended.
Point Ky at an unreachable port on Node (Undici). Confirm the thrown error is `NetworkError`. Confirm `error.cause.message === 'fetch failed'` and that GET is retried up to `limit`.
Make a request with an `AbortController` and abort it. Confirm the `AbortError` passes through unwrapped and is not retried.
Trigger a timeout with `retryOnTimeout: true`. Confirm Ky still throws `TimeoutError` and does not wrap it, even though the timeout is now inside the new `try/catch`.
Throw `TypeError('Load failed')` with a stack from a custom `fetch`. Confirm Ky does not wrap or retry it. Repeat with the stack deleted and confirm Ky wraps it in `NetworkError`.
Call `isNetworkError(new DOMException('x', 'NetworkError'))` and `isKyError` on the same value. Confirm the results are acceptable.
Check the changelog or release notes for a breaking-change entry about `TypeError` becoming `NetworkError` and about unknown errors no longer being retried.
